paragraphs: Here's what I see in this one, friend. Gideon is scared, and he knows it. He asks for the fleece, then asks AGAIN, and he says, "Do not be angry with me; let me speak one more time." (Judges 6:39) God doesn't walk off. He does it, and the fleece is dry and the ground is wet, just like Gideon asked (Judges 6:40).

Then the LORD does the math, and it makes no sense to me. He says, "You have too many men for Me to deliver Midian into their hands, lest Israel glorify themselves over Me, saying, 'My own hand has saved me.'" (Judges 7:2) Twenty-two thousand go home, then the rest get sifted down to three hundred (Judges 7:3, 6). I've counted cookies my whole life, and I would NEVER cut the batch down to three hundred, but the LORD wants the credit to land in the right place.

So here's the big idea for you, baker. You don't have to be strong enough, loud enough or sure enough, because the LORD said, "With the three hundred men who lapped the water I will save you." (Judges 7:7) When you feel like a small batch against a huge valley, He is the One who does the saving. Gideon's story isn't over, so keep the oven warm.
